transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Veritas CTO), Mark D'Souza (Veritas ML Eng), Priya Patel (Veritas Product)

---
Summary (auto): quick hosted api demo focusing on chat and text generation basics, streaming, parameters, retries.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya with redwood inference — i'm the AE on this account, with liam our se who will walk through the demo. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: good thanks, excited to see this — we are evaluating hosted options for our triage assistant, latency is a big one for us.
[00:15] Liam: awesome, yeah i'll keep that in mind — i'll show streaming and how we tune params and also touch on retries/backoff.
[00:22] Priya: quick note, we have some PHI-ish examples but we'll scrub for this call.
[00:28] Maya: perfect, thank you. so agenda: quick intro, live demo of hosted api (chat + text gen), parameters, streaming, retries + error handling, and then security/Q&A.
[01:05] Liam: ok switching to the console — just to be clear this is the hosted api, same endpoints you call via rest or sdk. first example: a turn-based chat call, we'll stream tokens back so the client can render partial responses. so request looks like messages array, model, and streaming flag.
[01:30] Mark: what does streaming latency look like? like first token to first byte?
[01:36] Liam: great question — first byte is typically 50-150ms on our hosted regions for models like redwood-7b-1 (depending on tokenization and prompt size). there's variance, so we expose token-level timing in the console for debugging.
[01:55] Aisha: are those numbers with or without prefix caching?
[01:58] Liam: that's without cache; with prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts we often shave 30-60% off tail latency. for triage flows where prompts share prefixes it's super helpful.
[02:20] Maya: also we provide recommended batching settings and a sample library for client-side buffer so you can trade off cost vs latency.
[02:35] Priya: can you show an example of params? like temperature and stop sequences?
[02:40] Liam: sure — here in the example call i set max_tokens=256, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, presence_penalty=0.0. stop can be a string or array; for chat it's common to use role tags.
[03:05] Maya: one thing customers ask — deterministic output for certain flows. if you need that you use temperature=0 and top_p=1 and also pin model version.
[03:20] Mark: if we set temperature 0 how do you handle safety filters? we have filters at our side but want to keep safe generation.
[03:29] Liam: safety is orthogonal — we have content-moderation endpoints and you can pipe outputs through your own checks. we also have a configurable policy for flagged responses in enterprise plans.
[03:52] Maya: short interjection — re: retries, our SDK does exponential backoff with jitter by default. we recommend idempotency keys on create calls when you might retry generating the same user message.
[04:10] Priya: idempotency for generation? can you expand — we usually de-dupe on our side but want to keep UX smooth.
[04:18] Liam: yeah, for non-streamed generation you re-use the idempotency key so if a network blip happens the server knows it's the same request and won't bill twice. for streamed responses it's trickier — we recommend client reconnection logic to resume, and server-side tokens are ephemeral.
[04:45] [short crosstalk] Speaker 2: okay.
[04:55] Liam: demo time — i'll send a streaming chat request live. note there's a small transcript lag in the recording.
[05:12] [05:12] Liam: (typing) sending request... [05:17] Liam: we get the first bytes back, watch how messages render in the UI as tokens arrive.
[05:40] Aisha: nice, that felt snappy. how do we set timeouts on client side? we have mobile clients where we want 2s max to first byte.
[05:50] Liam: you can set request-level timeouts and partial-render thresholds. if you need ultra-low first byte we recommend a model variant optimized for latency and smaller context length.
[06:10] Mark: variant meaning quantized or different model size?
[06:15] Liam: both — model size (e.g., 7B vs 13B) and execution profiles (int8 quantized variants) change latency/cost. in hosted we offer redwood-7b-1-int8-ish variants and you can route by policy.
[06:34] Priya: curious about pricing — cost per token? and streaming vs non-streaming differences?
[06:40] Maya: pricing is per output/input token; streaming doesn't change pricing model, it's just a different transport. we can send a pricing sheet after.
[06:54] Aisha: security: we need SSO + audit logs + KMS. is that available on hosted?
[07:02] Maya: yes — hosted supports SAML/SSO for the console, audit logs in enterprise tiers, and we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we offer tenant encryption at rest and BYOK options depending on contract. we'll share the SOC2 and security whitepaper.
[07:30] Mark: data residency — some of our users are EU-based and we need data to stay in region.
[07:36] Liam: we have region controls for hosted and can pin requests to EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[07:50] Priya: quick demo of retries — is that visible in the console?
[07:55] Liam: yes, retry events and per-request timing visible in the request trace. here's an example where we simulated a transient error and the SDK retried with exponential backoff.
[08:20] [08:20] Liam: (shares code) /* pseudo */ client.generate({ model: 'redwood-7b-1', messages, stream: true, timeout: 8000 })
[08:35] Maya: one common pattern is to do a low-latency fast path (smaller model) and fall back to higher-quality model if the first doesn't meet criteria. we call that smart routing or tiered fallbacks.
[08:55] Aisha: can that be automated? we don't want lots of conditional logic in product.
[09:02] Liam: yes — you can declare routing policies by latency or cost thresholds; platform will try primary and if it times out fall back. it's part of Redwood's smart routing.
[09:24] Mark: about request rate — our peak QPS might be 120 requests/s with bursts. how does hosted handle that?
[09:32] Liam: hosted has per-account rate limits and throttling; you can request rate increases. for predictable large throughput we recommend Dedicated where you can reserve capacity.
[09:48] Priya: any guidance on batching? we have multiple small prompts per user, wondering if batching at the gateway is worth it.
[09:56] Liam: batching is great for throughput but increases latency for first byte; we have an optimize tool to recommend batching windows based on your latency SLOs. small batches or asynchronous aggregation often works.
[10:18] Aisha: is there a demo of Redwood Optimize we can see?
[10:22] Maya: we can share a short Optimize walkthrough in follow-up — it shows batching/caching suggestions and quantization recommendations.
[10:35] Mark: about model version pinning — if you pin a model and we want a newer one later can we A/B?
[10:40] Liam: yes, rollouts and A/B are supported; you can target by percentage and compare latency/cost and qualitative evals.
[10:58] Priya: can we integrate evals in our CI? like run prompt sets against a model and alert on regressions?
[11:05] Liam: absolutely — we have an evals pipeline and can tie regression alerts to prompt sets. many customers run nightly checks.
[11:25] [short pause] Speaker 3: 
[11:40] Aisha: one more security — retention policies and ability to opt-out of logging payloads? we need to ensure PHI is not stored.
[11:48] Maya: hosted has configurable retention and we offer a no-logging option for certain enterprise contracts; for full control dedicated or private gives you the strictest guarantees. we'll include a matrix in the security doc.
[12:10] Mark: okay can we do a quick live example of parameter tuning? maybe show how changing temperature affects output.
[12:16] Liam: sure — example 1 temp 0.0, example 2 temp 0.8. i'll run both (non-streamed to keep it simple).
[12:40] [12:40] Liam: example low temp: output is very deterministic, short, conservative. example high temp: more creative, longer.
[13:05] Priya: that was helpful — for triage we want conservative so lower temp plus stop tokens.
[13:15] Maya: right. also presence_penalty helps avoid re-hashing same things.
[13:30] Mark: re: retries and billing — you mentioned idempotency prevents double billing? how reliable is that?
[13:38] Liam: if you retry with same idempotency key the platform dedupes the compute. network-level duplicates might still be possible but dedupe covers server processing.
[13:55] Aisha: do you offer SDKs for mobile? we have iOS and Android apps.
[14:00] Liam: yes, we have lightweight SDKs and recommend server-side gateway for auth tokens to avoid exposing keys.
[14:12] Priya: can you show request/response schema once?
[14:15] Liam: sure i pasted it in chat — messages array, each message has role and content, model field, optional params: temperature, max_tokens, top_p, stream flag, idempotency_key.
[14:42] [14:42] Maya: quick sales note — typical next step we see is a short POC 2-4 weeks where we run a benchmark with your prompt set and measure latency/cost and fidelity.
[14:55] Mark: that works. what do you need from us?
[14:59] Maya: sample prompts, target latency and QPS, and a small set of judges for subjective evals.
[15:10] Aisha: we'll get that to you — Mark will own prompts.
[15:15] Mark: sure.
[15:20] Liam: back to streaming — network reconnections: our client generates a resume token on interruption and you can re-request from last acked token. that's in our advanced SDKs.
[15:40] Priya: edge case: duplicate tokens on resume?
[15:44] Liam: some duplication is possible; client-side dedupe on token ids recommended. we can share library code.
[16:02] [short laughter]
[16:10] Aisha: for SOC2 evidence request — can you provide SOC2 report and typical attestation scope?
[16:18] Maya: yes we'll send the SOC2 type II and a summary of controls; larger customers get attestation packages.
[16:30] Mark: one more: can we pin requests to EU region and still use hosted?
[16:36] Liam: yes, region pinning available on hosted; again Dedicated/Private for stricter requirements.
[16:50] Priya: what about SDK retries config? is it customizable?
[16:54] Liam: full control — you can tweak backoff params, jitter, and max attempts. we default to conservative values.
[17:10] Maya: okay let's do a short recap and next steps.
[17:15] Maya: recap: demoed streaming chat, params, retries, and discussed security and routing. next steps are Maya sends pricing and security docs, Liam prepares POC checklist, Mark shares prompts and QPS, Priya confirms stakeholders.
[17:33] Aisha: timeline — can we aim for POC the week of apr 6?
[17:38] Maya: yes, that's doable — we'll coordinate calendar invites after this.
[17:45] Mark: fine by me.
[17:50] Priya: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[17:55] Maya: thanks all, i'll follow up with the docs.
[18:05] [call ends — note recording continues a few seconds then stops]
